# Consistency of OLS

## OLS in terms of sample averages

::: {.hidden}
\gdef\E#1{\mathrm{E}\left[#1\right]}
\gdef\Var#1{\mathrm{Var}\left(#1\right)}
\gdef\Cov#1{\mathrm{Cov}\left(#1\right)}
\gdef\rank#1{\operatorname{rank}\left(#1\right)}
:::

- Regression, $\{(Y_i, X_i) : i = 1, \ldots, n\}$ iid:
  $$
  Y_i = X_i^\top \beta + U_i, \qquad \underset{k\times1}{X_i} = \begin{pmatrix} X_{i,1} \\ \vdots \\ X_{i,k} \end{pmatrix}
  $$

- OLS from $n$ observations, $\rank{X} = k$ (Lecture 1); substitute $Y_i = X_i^\top \beta + U_i$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat\beta_n &= (X^\top X)^{-1} X^\top Y \\
  &= \Big(\underbrace{\sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top}_{k\times k}\Big)^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i Y_i \\
  &= \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i \big(X_i^\top \beta + U_i\big) \\
  &= \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big) \beta + \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i \\
  &= \beta + \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i \\
  &= \beta + \Big({\color{red}\frac{1}{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} {\color{red}\frac{1}{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Squares and cross-products:
  $$
  \underset{k\times k}{X_i X_i^\top} = \begin{pmatrix} X_{i,1}^2 & X_{i,1} X_{i,2} & \cdots & X_{i,1} X_{i,k} \\ X_{i,2} X_{i,1} & X_{i,2}^2 & \cdots & X_{i,2} X_{i,k} \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ X_{i,k} X_{i,1} & X_{i,k} X_{i,2} & \cdots & X_{i,k}^2 \end{pmatrix}
  $$

- Element $(r, s)$:
  $$
  \Big[\sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big]_{rs} = \sum_{i=1}^n X_{i,r} X_{i,s}
  $$

## LLN for $\frac{1}{n} \sum X_i U_i$

- $X_1 U_1, \ldots, X_n U_n$: iid; weak LLN, element by element:
  $$
  \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i \to_p \E{X_i U_i}
  $$

- **Assume:**
  $$
  \E{X_i U_i} = 0
  $$

- Weak LLN for element $j$ requires:
  $$
  \E{|X_{i,j} U_i|} < \infty, \qquad j = 1, \ldots, k
  $$

- Cauchy-Schwarz inequality:
  $$
  \E{|X_{i,j} U_i|} \le \sqrt{\E{X_{i,j}^2}\, \E{U_i^2}}
  $$

- **Assume:**
  $$
  \E{U_i^2} < \infty, \qquad \E{X_{i,j}^2} < \infty, \quad j = 1, \ldots, k
  $$

## LLN for $\frac{1}{n} \sum X_i X_i^\top$

- Element $(r, s)$ of $\E{X_i X_i^\top}$ well defined, Cauchy-Schwarz:
  $$
  \E{|X_{i,r} X_{i,s}|} \le \sqrt{\E{X_{i,r}^2}\, \E{X_{i,s}^2}} < \infty
  $$

- Weak LLN, element by element:
  $$
  \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top \to_p \E{X_i X_i^\top}
  $$

- $\E{X_i X_i^\top}$: symmetric, p.s.d.

- **Assume:**
  $$
  \E{X_i X_i^\top} \ \text{ p.d.}
  $$

- Slutsky, $h(\cdot) = (\cdot)^{-1}$ continuous at a p.d. matrix (Lecture 8):
  $$
  \Big(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \to_p \big(\E{X_i X_i^\top}\big)^{-1}
  $$

## Assumptions

- Assumptions for consistency:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & \{(Y_i, X_i) : i = 1, \ldots, n\} \ \text{ iid} \\
  & Y_i = X_i^\top \beta + U_i \\
  & \E{X_i U_i} = 0 \\
  & \E{U_i^2} < \infty \\
  & \E{X_{i,j}^2} < \infty, \quad j = 1, \ldots, k \\
  & \E{X_i X_i^\top} \ \text{ p.d. (no perfect multicollinearity)}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $U_i = Y_i - X_i^\top \beta$:
  $$
  \{(Y_i, X_i)\} \ \text{ iid} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \{(U_i, X_i)\} \ \text{ iid}
  $$

- $(Y_1, X_1)$ independent of $(Y_2, X_2)$; $Y_1$ and $X_1$ need not be independent.

- Weaker than $\E{U_i \mid X_i} = 0$:
  $$
  \E{X_i U_i} = 0 \quad \nRightarrow \quad \E{Y_i \mid X_i} = X_i^\top \beta \quad \text{(in general)}
  $$

## Consistency

- **Definition.** $\hat\beta_n$ is a consistent estimator of $\beta$ if $\hat\beta_n \to_p \beta$.

- Element by element, by definition (Lecture 8):
  $$
  \hat\beta_n \to_p \beta \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \hat\beta_{n,j} \to_p \beta_j, \quad j = 1, \ldots, k
  $$

- **Theorem.** Under the assumptions for consistency, $\hat\beta_n \to_p \beta$.

- The two limits, then Slutsky for the product:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat\beta_n &= \beta + \Big(\underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top}_{\to_p\, \E{X_i X_i^\top}}\Big)^{-1} \underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i}_{\to_p\, 0} \\
  &\to_p \beta + \big(\E{X_i X_i^\top}\big)^{-1} \cdot 0 \\
  &= \beta
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Therefore:
  $$
  \boxed{\ \hat\beta_n \to_p \beta\ }
  $$

# Asymptotic normality of OLS

## Assumptions I and II

- $\hat\beta_n - \beta \to_p 0$. Approximate the distribution of $\hat\beta_n - \beta$: scale by $\sqrt{n}$ (Lecture 8).

- **Assumption I.**
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & \{(Y_i, X_i) : i = 1, \ldots, n\} \ \text{ iid} \\
  & Y_i = X_i^\top \beta + U_i, \qquad \beta \in \mathbb{R}^k
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- OLS:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat\beta_n &= \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i Y_i \\
  &= \beta + \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad \hat\beta_n - \beta &= \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- **Assumption II.**
  $$
  \underset{k\times k}{Q} = \E{X_i X_i^\top} \quad \text{p.d. and finite}
  $$

- Weak LLN, then Slutsky:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top &\to_p \E{X_i X_i^\top} = Q \\
  \Big(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} &\to_p Q^{-1} = \big(\E{X_i X_i^\top}\big)^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Scaling by $\sqrt{n}$

- Multiply by $\sqrt{n}$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  {\color{red}\sqrt{n}}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) &= \sqrt{n} \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i \\
  &= \sqrt{n} \Big(n \cdot \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i \\
  &= \frac{\sqrt{n}}{n} \Big(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i \\
  &= \Big({\color{red}\frac{1}{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} {\color{red}\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Assumption III and the CLT

- **Assumption III.**
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & \E{X_i U_i} = 0 \quad \text{($X$'s and $U$'s uncorrelated)} \\
  & \underset{k\times k}{\Omega} = \Var{X_i U_i} \quad \text{finite and p.d.}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Variance of $X_i U_i$, with $\E{X_i U_i} = 0$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Omega &= \Var{X_i U_i} \\
  &= \E{X_i U_i (X_i U_i)^\top} \\
  &= \E{X_i \underset{1\times1}{U_i}\, \underset{1\times1}{U_i} X_i^\top} \\
  &= \E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $X_1 U_1, \ldots, X_n U_n$: iid $k \times 1$ (Assumption I), mean $0$, variance $\Omega$ finite and p.d. (Assumption III).

- Multivariate CLT (Lecture 8):
  $$
  \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i \to_d N\big(0,\ \underbrace{\E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top}}_{\Omega}\big)
  $$

## Limit of $\sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta)$

- We will use, without proof (Cramér convergence theorem): $A_n \to_p A$, $A$ non-random, and $Z_n \to_d Z$:
  $$
  A_n Z_n \to_d A Z
  $$

- The two limits:
  $$
  {\color{red}\sqrt{n}}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) = \underbrace{\Big({\color{red}\frac{1}{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1}}_{\to_p\, Q^{-1}} \underbrace{{\color{red}\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i}_{\to_d\, N(0,\, \Omega)} \to_d Q^{-1} N(0, \Omega)
  $$

- Linear map of a normal vector (Lecture 4):
  $$
  W \sim N(\mu, \Sigma) \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \Gamma W \sim N(\Gamma \mu,\ \Gamma \Sigma \Gamma^\top)
  $$

- $\Gamma = Q^{-1}$; $Q = \E{X_i X_i^\top} = Q^\top$, so $(Q^{-1})^\top = Q^{-1}$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  Q^{-1} N(0, \Omega) &\overset{d}{=} N\big(Q^{-1} \cdot 0,\ Q^{-1} \Omega (Q^{-1})^\top\big) \\
  &= N\big(0,\ Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1}\big)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Asymptotic variance

- **Theorem.** Under Assumptions I to III:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & \boxed{\ \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \to_d N\Big(0,\ \underbrace{\big(\E{X_i X_i^\top}\big)^{-1} \E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top} \big(\E{X_i X_i^\top}\big)^{-1}}_{\mathrm{AsyVar}(\hat\beta_n)}\Big)\ } \\
  & \mathrm{AsyVar}(\hat\beta_n) = Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1} \quad \text{(sandwich)}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- CDF form, for all $a \ne 0$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}$:
  $$
  \mathrm{P}\big(a^\top \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \le t\big) \to \Phi\Big(\frac{t}{\sqrt{a^\top Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1} a}}\Big)
  $$

- $a = e_j$, element $j$:
  $$
  \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j) \to_d N\big(0,\ [Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1}]_{jj}\big)
  $$

## Homoskedasticity

- Suppose:
  $$
  \E{U_i^2 \mid X_i} = \sigma^2 \quad \text{(homoskedasticity)}
  $$

- Law of iterated expectations:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Omega &= \E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top} \\
  &= \E{\E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top \mid X_i}} \\
  &= \E{\underbrace{\E{U_i^2 \mid X_i}}_{=\,\sigma^2} X_i X_i^\top} \\
  &= \sigma^2 \E{X_i X_i^\top} \\
  &= \sigma^2 Q
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- The sandwich collapses:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \mathrm{AsyVar}(\hat\beta_n) &= Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1} \\
  &= Q^{-1} (\sigma^2 Q) Q^{-1} \\
  &= \sigma^2 Q^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Therefore:
  $$
  \boxed{\ \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \to_d N\Big(0,\ \sigma^2 \big(\E{X_i X_i^\top}\big)^{-1}\Big)\ }
  $$

## Finite sample against large sample

- Normal errors (Lecture 4, Assumptions 1 to 5), exact for every $n$ (requires stronger assumptions), $a \ne 0$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & Y = X\beta + U, \qquad U \mid X \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I_n) \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & \hat\beta_n \mid X \sim N\big(\beta,\ \sigma^2 (X^\top X)^{-1}\big) \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & \mathrm{P}\big(a^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta) \le t \mid X\big) = \Phi\Big(\frac{t}{\sqrt{\sigma^2 a^\top (X^\top X)^{-1} a}}\Big)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Homoskedastic errors, large sample, $a \ne 0$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & \text{Assumptions I and II}, \quad \E{X_i U_i} = 0, \quad \E{U_i^2 \mid X_i} = \sigma^2 > 0 \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & \mathrm{P}\big(a^\top \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \le t\big) \to \Phi\Big(\frac{t}{\sqrt{\sigma^2 a^\top \big(\E{X_i X_i^\top}\big)^{-1} a}}\Big)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- General, large sample, $a \ne 0$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & \text{Assumptions I to III}; \quad Q = \E{X_i X_i^\top}, \quad \Omega = \E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top} \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & \mathrm{P}\big(a^\top \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \le t\big) \to \Phi\Big(\frac{t}{\sqrt{a^\top Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1} a}}\Big)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

# Estimation of the asymptotic variance

## The estimator $\hat V_n$

- Unknown:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  V &= \mathrm{AsyVar}(\hat\beta_n) = Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1} \\
  Q &= \E{X_i X_i^\top}, \qquad \Omega = \E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Estimator, sample averages in place of expectations:
  $$
  \hat V_n = \hat Q_n^{-1} \hat\Omega_n \hat Q_n^{-1}
  $$

- $\hat Q_n$: weak LLN, then Slutsky (Assumption II):
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat Q_n &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top \to_p \E{X_i X_i^\top} = Q \\
  \hat Q_n^{-1} &\to_p Q^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $\hat\Omega_n$, residuals $\hat U_i$ in place of $U_i$:
  $$
  \hat\Omega_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top
  $$

- Residual and error, $i$ fixed (continuous mapping theorem, without proof):
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat U_i &= Y_i - X_i^\top \hat\beta_n \\
  &= X_i^\top \beta + U_i - X_i^\top \hat\beta_n \\
  &= U_i + X_i^\top \underbrace{(\beta - \hat\beta_n)}_{\to_p\, 0} \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad \hat U_i &\to_p U_i \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad \hat U_1^2 + \hat U_2^2 &\to_p U_1^2 + U_2^2
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Can we use the LLN on $\hat\Omega_n$?

- **Definition.** Small $o_p$:
  $$
  Z_n = o_p(1) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad Z_n \to_p 0
  $$

- One $o_p(1)$ term for each $i$, $\hat U_i = U_i + o_p^i(1)$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat\Omega_n &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top \\
  &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(U_i + o_p^i(1)\big)^2 X_i X_i^\top \\
  &\overset{?}{=} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top + o_p(1)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $\sum_{i=1}^n o_p^i(1)$ can be large.

- Weak LLN? Summands not iid:
  $$
  \hat U_i = U_i - X_i^\top \underbrace{(\hat\beta_n - \beta)}_{\text{random}}
  $$

- $\hat U_1$ and $\hat U_2$: correlated via $\hat\beta_n$.

## Matrix norm

- To show:
  $$
  \hat\Omega_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top \to_p \E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top} = \Omega, \qquad \underset{k\times k}{\Omega}, \ \ \underset{k\times k}{X_i X_i^\top}
  $$

- Frobenius norm, $\underset{k\times k}{A}$ (Euclidean norm of the $k^2$ elements):
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \|A\| &= \sqrt{\sum_{r=1}^k \sum_{s=1}^k A_{rs}^2} \\
  &= \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(A^\top A)}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Element by element $\Longleftrightarrow$ in norm (Lecture 8); to show:
  $$
  \|\underbrace{\hat\Omega_n - \Omega}_{k\times k}\| \to_p 0
  $$

## Expansion of $\hat\Omega_n$

- Substitute $\hat U_i = U_i - X_i^\top(\hat\beta_n - \beta)$; square, $(a - b)^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat\Omega_n &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top \\
  &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(\underbrace{Y_i - X_i^\top \hat\beta_n}_{\hat U_i}\big)^2 X_i X_i^\top \\
  &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(U_i - \underbrace{X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)}_{1\times1}\big)^2 X_i X_i^\top \\
  &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \Big(U_i^2 + \big(X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big)^2 - 2\, U_i X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\Big) X_i X_i^\top \\
  &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top + \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big)^2 X_i X_i^\top \\
  &\qquad - 2\, \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(U_i X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big) X_i X_i^\top
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- First term, weak LLN, $\Omega$ finite (Assumption III):
  $$
  \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top \to_p \E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top} = \Omega
  $$

- To show: the other two terms $\to_p 0$.

## Cross term: triangle inequality

- Triangle inequality, $\|a + b\| \le \|a\| + \|b\|$; then $\|cA\| = |c|\, \|A\|$ for $1 \times 1$ $c$; then $|a b| = |a|\, |b|$ for $1 \times 1$ $a$, $b$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Big\|\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(U_i X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big) \underset{k\times k}{X_i X_i^\top}\Big\| &\le \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \Big\|\underbrace{\big(U_i X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big)}_{1\times1} X_i X_i^\top\Big\| \\
  &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big|U_i X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big|\, \|X_i X_i^\top\| \\
  &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n |U_i|\, \big|X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big|\, \|X_i X_i^\top\|
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Cauchy-Schwarz and $\|X_i X_i^\top\|$

- Cauchy-Schwarz:
  $$
  \big|X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big| \le \|X_i\|\, \|\hat\beta_n - \beta\|
  $$

- $\underset{k\times k}{A} = X_i X_i^\top = A^\top$; $\operatorname{tr}(BC) = \operatorname{tr}(CB)$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \|X_i X_i^\top\| &= \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}\big(\underbrace{X_i X_i^\top}_{A^\top} \underbrace{X_i X_i^\top}_{A}\big)} \\
  &= \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}\big(X_i \underbrace{X_i^\top X_i}_{=\,\|X_i\|^2} X_i^\top\big)} \\
  &= \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}\big(X_i \underbrace{\|X_i\|^2}_{1\times1} X_i^\top\big)} \\
  &= \sqrt{\|X_i\|^2 \operatorname{tr}\big(X_i X_i^\top\big)} \\
  &= \|X_i\| \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}\big(X_i X_i^\top\big)} \\
  &= \|X_i\| \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}\big(X_i^\top X_i\big)} \\
  &= \|X_i\| \sqrt{\|X_i\|^2} \\
  &= \|X_i\|^2
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Cross term $\to_p 0$

- Cauchy-Schwarz and $\|X_i X_i^\top\| = \|X_i\|^2$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \underbrace{\Big\|\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(U_i X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big) X_i X_i^\top\Big\|}_{1\times1} &\le \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n |U_i|\, \big|X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big|\, \|X_i X_i^\top\| \\
  &\le \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \underset{1\times1}{|U_i|}\, \underset{1\times1}{\|X_i\|}\, \underset{1\times1}{\|\hat\beta_n - \beta\|}\, \underset{1\times1}{\|X_i\|^2} \\
  &= \Big(\underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n |U_i|\, \|X_i\|^3}_{\to_p\, \E{|U_i|\, \|X_i\|^3}}\Big) \cdot \underbrace{\|\hat\beta_n - \beta\|}_{\to_p\, 0}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Weak LLN, provided $\E{|U_i|\, \|X_i\|^3} < \infty$. Cauchy-Schwarz twice:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \E{|U_i|\, \|X_i\|^3} &= \E{|U_i|\, \|X_i\| \cdot \|X_i\|^2} \\
  &\le \sqrt{\E{U_i^2 \|X_i\|^2}\, \E{\|X_i\|^4}} \\
  &\le \sqrt{\sqrt{\E{U_i^4}\, \E{\|X_i\|^4}} \cdot \E{\|X_i\|^4}}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- **Assume:**
  $$
  \E{U_i^4} < \infty, \qquad \E{\|X_i\|^4} < \infty
  $$

- Slutsky, bound $\to_p 0$; non-negative norm:
  $$
  \Big\|\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(U_i X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big) X_i X_i^\top\Big\| \to_p 0
  $$

## Squared term $\to_p 0$

- Triangle inequality and $\|cA\| = |c|\, \|A\|$, then Cauchy-Schwarz and $\|X_i X_i^\top\| = \|X_i\|^2$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Big\|\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(\underbrace{X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)}_{1\times1}\big)^2 X_i X_i^\top\Big\| &\le \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big)^2\, \|X_i X_i^\top\| \\
  &\le \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \|X_i\|^2\, \|\hat\beta_n - \beta\|^2\, \|X_i\|^2 \\
  &= \Big(\underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \|X_i\|^4}_{\to_p\, \E{\|X_i\|^4} < \infty}\Big) \cdot \underbrace{\|\hat\beta_n - \beta\|^2}_{\to_p\, 0}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Slutsky, bound $\to_p 0$; non-negative norm:
  $$
  \Big\|\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big)^2 X_i X_i^\top\Big\| \to_p 0
  $$

## $\hat\Omega_n \to_p \Omega$ and $\hat V_n \to_p V$

- Three terms:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat\Omega_n &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top \\
  &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top + \underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big)^2 X_i X_i^\top}_{{\color{red}\to_p\, 0}} \\
  &\qquad - 2\, \underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(U_i X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big) X_i X_i^\top}_{{\color{red}\to_p\, 0}} \\
  &= \underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top}_{\to_p\, \E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top} = \Omega} {}+ o_p(1) \\
  &\to_p \Omega
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- **Theorem.** Under Assumptions I to III, $\E{U_i^4} < \infty$ and $\E{\|X_i\|^4} < \infty$, with or without homoskedasticity:
  $$
  \boxed{\ \hat V_n = \hat Q_n^{-1} \hat\Omega_n \hat Q_n^{-1} \to_p Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1} = V\ } \quad \text{(Slutsky, $\hat Q_n^{-1} \to_p Q^{-1}$)}
  $$

# Robust and usual standard errors

## Robust standard errors

- $\overset{a}{\sim}$: approximately distributed, for large $n$:
  $$
  \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \overset{a}{\sim} N(0, V) \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \hat\beta_{n,j} \overset{a}{\sim} N\Big(\beta_j,\ \frac{[V]_{jj}}{n}\Big)
  $$

- **Definition.** Robust (heteroskedasticity-consistent, White) standard error; $\hat Q_n = \frac{1}{n} X^\top X$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big) &= \sqrt{[\hat V_n]_{jj} / n} \\
  &= \sqrt{\Big[\frac{1}{n} \Big(\frac{1}{n} X^\top X\Big)^{-1} \Big(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top\Big) \Big(\frac{1}{n} X^\top X\Big)^{-1}\Big]_{jj}} \\
  &= \sqrt{\Big[\frac{1}{n} \cdot n (X^\top X)^{-1} \cdot \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top \cdot n (X^\top X)^{-1}\Big]_{jj}} \\
  &= \sqrt{\Big[(X^\top X)^{-1} \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top\Big) (X^\top X)^{-1}\Big]_{jj}}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Lecture 2, heteroskedastic errors, $\Var{U_i \mid X} = \sigma_i^2$; $\hat U_i^2$ in place of $\sigma_i^2$:
  $$
  \Var{\hat\beta \mid X} = (X^\top X)^{-1} \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n \sigma_i^2 X_i X_i^\top\Big) (X^\top X)^{-1}
  $$

## $t$-ratio with robust standard errors

- We will use, without proof (Cramér convergence theorem): $Z_n \to_d Z$, $c_n \to_p c \ne 0$, $c$ non-random:
  $$
  \frac{Z_n}{c_n} \to_d \frac{Z}{c}
  $$

- Slutsky, $\sqrt{[\hat V_n]_{jj}} \to_p \sqrt{[V]_{jj}} > 0$ ($V$ p.d.); $\sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j) \to_d N(0, [V]_{jj})$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \frac{\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j}{\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)} &= \frac{\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j}{\sqrt{[\hat V_n]_{jj} / n}} \\
  &= \frac{\sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j)}{\sqrt{[\hat V_n]_{jj}}} \\
  &\to_d \frac{N\big(0, [V]_{jj}\big)}{\sqrt{[V]_{jj}}} \\
  &\overset{d}{=} N(0, 1)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Asymptotic confidence interval:
  $$
  CI_{1-\alpha} = \Big[\hat\beta_{n,j} - z_{1-\alpha/2}\, \text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big),\ \hat\beta_{n,j} + z_{1-\alpha/2}\, \text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)\Big]
  $$

- Coverage, $t$-ratio $\to_d Z \sim N(0, 1)$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \mathrm{P}\big(\beta_j \in CI_{1-\alpha}\big) &= \mathrm{P}\Big(\Big|\frac{\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j}{\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)}\Big| \le z_{1-\alpha/2}\Big) \\
  &\to \mathrm{P}\big(|Z| \le z_{1-\alpha/2}\big) \\
  &= 1 - \alpha
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Usual standard errors

- Lecture 3:
  $$
  \text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big) = \sqrt{s^2 \big[(X^\top X)^{-1}\big]_{jj}}, \qquad s^2 = \frac{1}{n - k} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2
  $$

- In terms of $\hat Q_n = \frac{1}{n} X^\top X$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  s^2 (X^\top X)^{-1} &= \frac{1}{n}\, s^2 \Big(\frac{1}{n} X^\top X\Big)^{-1} \\
  &= \frac{1}{n}\, s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Usual: $s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1}$, built for $\sigma^2 Q^{-1}$ (homoskedasticity); robust: $\hat V_n$, for $V$:
  $$
  \text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big) = \sqrt{[s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1}]_{jj} / n}, \qquad \text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big) = \sqrt{[\hat V_n]_{jj} / n}
  $$

## $s^2 \to_p \E{U_i^2}$

- $\hat U_i = U_i - X_i^\top(\hat\beta_n - \beta)$; $U_i X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta) = (\hat\beta_n - \beta)^\top X_i U_i$; $\E{U_i^2} \le \sqrt{\E{U_i^4}} < \infty$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(U_i - X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big)^2 \\
  &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2 - 2\, \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta) + \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big)^2 \\
  &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2 - 2\, (\hat\beta_n - \beta)^\top \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i + (\hat\beta_n - \beta)^\top \Big(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big) (\hat\beta_n - \beta) \\
  &\to_p \E{U_i^2} - 2 \cdot 0^\top 0 + 0^\top Q\, 0 \quad \text{(weak LLN, consistency, Slutsky)} \\
  &= \E{U_i^2}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $\frac{n}{n - k} \to 1$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  s^2 &= \frac{n}{n - k} \cdot \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 \\
  &\to_p 1 \cdot \E{U_i^2} = \E{U_i^2}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Homoskedasticity, law of iterated expectations:
  $$
  \E{U_i^2} = \E{\E{U_i^2 \mid X_i}} = \sigma^2
  $$

## Homoskedasticity: robust and usual agree

- Both estimators of $\mathrm{AsyVar}(\hat\beta_n) = \sigma^2 Q^{-1}$ consistent:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat V_n &\to_p Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1} = \sigma^2 Q^{-1} \\
  s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1} &\to_p \sigma^2 Q^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Ratio of the two standard errors, Slutsky, $\sigma^2 [Q^{-1}]_{jj} = [V]_{jj} > 0$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \frac{\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)}{\text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)} &= \sqrt{\frac{[\hat V_n]_{jj} / n}{[s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1}]_{jj} / n}} \\
  &= \sqrt{\frac{[\hat V_n]_{jj}}{[s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1}]_{jj}}} \\
  &\to_p \sqrt{\frac{\sigma^2 [Q^{-1}]_{jj}}{\sigma^2 [Q^{-1}]_{jj}}} \\
  &= 1
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Therefore:
  $$
  \boxed{\ \frac{\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)}{\text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)} \to_p 1\ }
  $$

- Usual $t$-ratio, $A_n Z_n \to_d A Z$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \frac{\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j}{\text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)} &= \underbrace{\frac{\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)}{\text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)}}_{\to_p\, 1} \cdot \underbrace{\frac{\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j}{\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)}}_{\to_d\, N(0, 1)} \\
  &\to_d N(0, 1)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Heteroskedasticity: usual standard errors fail

- Without homoskedasticity:
  $$
  s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1} \to_p \E{U_i^2}\, Q^{-1} \ne Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1} = V \quad \text{(in general)}
  $$

- Example, $k = 1$, no intercept: $Q = \E{X_i^2}$, $\Omega = \E{U_i^2 X_i^2}$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  V &= \frac{\E{U_i^2 X_i^2}}{\big(\E{X_i^2}\big)^2}, \qquad \text{usual: } \frac{\E{U_i^2}}{\E{X_i^2}} \\
  V - \frac{\E{U_i^2}}{\E{X_i^2}} &= \frac{\E{U_i^2 X_i^2} - \E{U_i^2}\, \E{X_i^2}}{\big(\E{X_i^2}\big)^2} \\
  &= \frac{\Cov{U_i^2, X_i^2}}{\big(\E{X_i^2}\big)^2}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $\Cov{U_i^2, X_i^2} > 0$, errors more variable where $|X_i|$ is large: usual standard error too small.

- Robust: $\hat V_n \to_p V$ with or without homoskedasticity.

## Normality: exact and asymptotic

- Normal errors (Lecture 4, Assumptions 1 to 5):
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & U \mid X \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I_n) \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & \hat\beta_n \mid X \sim N\big(\beta,\ \sigma^2 (X^\top X)^{-1}\big) \quad \text{for every } n
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Variance of $\sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta)$ given $X$, and its limit under Assumptions I and II:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Var{\sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \mid X} &= n\, \Var{\hat\beta_n \mid X} \\
  &= n\, \sigma^2 (X^\top X)^{-1} \\
  &= \sigma^2 \Big(\frac{1}{n} X^\top X\Big)^{-1} \\
  &= \sigma^2 \hat Q_n^{-1} \\
  &\to_p \sigma^2 Q^{-1} = \mathrm{AsyVar}(\hat\beta_n)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $\sigma^2$ estimated by $s^2$ (typed notes, Lecture 4):
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & \frac{\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j}{\text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)} \,\Big|\, X \sim t_{n-k} \quad \text{for every } n \\
  & t_{n-k,\,1-\alpha/2} \to z_{1-\alpha/2}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Normal errors are homoskedastic, so robust and usual agree in large samples ($\E{U_i^4} = 3\sigma^4$, $\E{\|X_i\|^4} < \infty$):
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \E{U_i^2 \mid X} &= \big[\sigma^2 I_n\big]_{ii} = \sigma^2 \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad \E{U_i^2 \mid X_i} &= \E{\E{U_i^2 \mid X} \mid X_i} = \sigma^2 \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad \frac{\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)}{\text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)} &\to_p 1
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Usual and robust standard errors compared

- Validity of the $t$-ratio (large $n$: conditions for $\hat V_n \to_p V$):

  | Errors | Usual std. err | Robust std. err |
  |---|---|---|
  | $U \mid X \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I_n)$ | exact, $t_{n-k}$ | large $n$, $N(0,1)$ |
  | $\E{U_i^2 \mid X_i} = \sigma^2$ | large $n$, $N(0,1)$ | large $n$, $N(0,1)$ |
  | $\E{U_i^2 \mid X_i}$ depends on $X_i$ | invalid in general | large $n$, $N(0,1)$ |

- Rows 1 and 2, $t_{n-k,\,1-\alpha/2} \to z_{1-\alpha/2}$ and $\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}} / \text{std. err} \to_p 1$; the three intervals agree in large samples:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \text{usual, exact (row 1):}\quad & \hat\beta_{n,j} \pm t_{n-k,\,1-\alpha/2}\, \text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big) \\
  \text{usual, large } n\text{:}\quad & \hat\beta_{n,j} \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\, \text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big) \\
  \text{robust, large } n\text{:}\quad & \hat\beta_{n,j} \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\, \text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

# Summary

## Consistency and asymptotic normality

- $\hat\beta_n = \beta + \big(\frac{1}{n} \sum X_i X_i^\top\big)^{-1} \frac{1}{n} \sum X_i U_i$; iid, $\E{X_i U_i} = 0$, $\E{U_i^2} < \infty$, $\E{X_{i,j}^2} < \infty$, $\E{X_i X_i^\top}$ p.d. $\Longrightarrow$ $\hat\beta_n \to_p \beta$.

- $\sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) = \big(\frac{1}{n} \sum X_i X_i^\top\big)^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum X_i U_i$.

- Assumptions I to III $\Longrightarrow$ $\sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \to_d N(0, Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1})$, $Q = \E{X_i X_i^\top}$, $\Omega = \E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top}$.

- $\E{U_i^2 \mid X_i} = \sigma^2$ $\Longrightarrow$ $\Omega = \sigma^2 Q$, $\mathrm{AsyVar}(\hat\beta_n) = \sigma^2 Q^{-1}$.

## Variance estimation and standard errors

- $\hat V_n = \hat Q_n^{-1} \hat\Omega_n \hat Q_n^{-1}$, $\hat Q_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum X_i X_i^\top$, $\hat\Omega_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top$.

- $\hat\Omega_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top + o_p(1)$ under Assumptions I to III, $\E{U_i^4} < \infty$, $\E{\|X_i\|^4} < \infty$; $\hat V_n \to_p V$.

- $\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}(\hat\beta_{n,j}) = \sqrt{\big[(X^\top X)^{-1} \big(\sum \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top\big) (X^\top X)^{-1}\big]_{jj}}$; $t$-ratio $\to_d N(0, 1)$; $\hat\beta_{n,j} \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\, \text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}$: coverage $\to 1 - \alpha$.

- $\text{std. err}(\hat\beta_{n,j}) = \sqrt{[s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1}]_{jj} / n}$, $s^2 \to_p \E{U_i^2}$; homoskedasticity: $\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}} / \text{std. err} \to_p 1$.

- Heteroskedasticity: $s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1} \to_p \E{U_i^2}\, Q^{-1} \ne V$ in general; only the robust standard error is always valid.

- Normality: $\Var{\sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \mid X} = \sigma^2 \hat Q_n^{-1} \to_p \sigma^2 Q^{-1}$; usual $t$-ratio exactly $t_{n-k}$, $t_{n-k,\,1-\alpha/2} \to z_{1-\alpha/2}$; homoskedastic, so $\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}} / \text{std. err} \to_p 1$.
